user_environment: Windows Codex desktop App; exact version and denied path not supplied
confirmed_installer_defect: Public program directories used mode 0700, which Windows Python maps to current-user/admin-only access controls.
fix: Use inherited parent ACL for Windows public program directories; managed upgrades recreate directories and nested runtime files. POSIX/private memory creation remains unchanged.

local_tests.skip_reason: Native Windows ACL test requires Windows

native_windows_ci.skips: Windows skips only the POSIX Bash command check; Ubuntu/macOS skip only native Windows ACL.

boundaries: Inherited ACL cannot override a restrictive parent or a managed permission profile.
Private memory ACLs and physical scope boundaries are not relaxed or relocated.
A host initialization UAC requirement is distinct from giving the AI administrator rights.
Normal installer execution is not evidence of sandbox process access.

findings: Non-UTF-8 pipe encoding broke Unicode installer receipts and paths.
Test fixture text reads/writes used a platform-dependent codec.
Some test fixtures assumed POSIX command lookup/path rendering/ZIP name normalization.
Native ACL post-upgrade assertion failed; diagnostic now records exact numeric rules without assuming inherited flags survive rename.
Unicode installation/runtime and fixture failures cleared.
ACL reader yielded null/empty data even for its parent; this is not valid ACL evidence. It now uses native .NET APIs and stops on errors.
Windows zipfile normalized raw backslashes during reading; validation now rejects names differing from orig_filename.

older_windows_python_boundary: The 3.10.11 CI build ignores 0700. Every tested version retains its original private ACL exactly; modern 3.14 reproduces and repairs the owner/admin-only legacy program ACL. Restrictiveness on older builds depends on the containing directory ACL.
